scope: Hashed struct, field and enum names in the PSIN metadata of common.rpf, script.rpf, data.rpf, levels.rpf and packs.rpf (GTA VI, Xbox build 1.0.2.1)

history.step: Case-sensitive hashing, the game's own strings
Public name lists from earlier RAGE games
levels.rpf and packs.rpf added (4,794 more names to find), name lists applied
Crack and judge on the wider set, second scan of the game text

accuracy.note: The exact text exists elsewhere; a chance collision is about 1 in 200,000 per name.

Accepted only where random decoy hashes show few chance matches; measured chance rate of a few percent. In a holdout test the cracker alone accepted 520 of 1,500 hidden known names: 518 right, 2 wrong (0.4%).

Holdout test on 1,260 hidden known names: 468 accepted, 458 right, 10 wrong (2.1%). On truly unknown names the same cut is estimated to be wrong about 8% of the time before judging; every such pick was then checked by a judge.

Picked by a language model from candidates that hash correctly. Holdout test: 1,500 known names were hidden and sent through the same cracker and judges, mixed with as many truly unknown ones. The judges accepted 196 hidden names: 195 right, 1 wrong (0.5%); where the true name was among the candidates they found it 80% of the time. The one wrong pick came from 580 lines that had no true candidate; scaled to the lines judged in the real rounds that is about 2% of the judged names, and one event leaves a wide range (well under 1% to about 11%). The hidden names come from older games and may be easier than the unknown ones.
